title: Heat Illness
summary: Overheated: heat exhaustion or heat stroke. Cool first, then get help.
sources: Wilderness Medical Society Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Prevention and Treatment of Heat Illness
firstLine: Get the person out of the sun and stop all activity now. Send someone to call for help if you can.

nodes.prompt: Are they confused, acting strangely, slurring, having a seizure, or not responding?
nodes.help: Any change in how they think or act, in a hot person, is heat stroke until proven otherwise. Skin may be wet or dry.

nodes.title: Heat stroke - cool them NOW
steps: Cool first, transport second. Every minute counts.
Best: put them in cold water up to the neck (stream, tub, tarp filled with water), holding their head above water.
If no immersion: strip excess clothing, soak them with water continuously, and fan hard. Wet sheets plus wind works well.
Put ice or cold packs on the neck, armpits, and groin as well, if you have them.
Keep cooling until their thinking clears or they start shivering. With a thermometer, stop at about 102 F (39 C).
doNot: Do not give fever medicine (acetaminophen, aspirin, ibuprofen). It does not help heat stroke and can cause harm.
Do not give anything to drink if they are confused or not fully awake.
Do not delay cooling to wait for transport.

options.label: Still confused or unresponsive, but breathing

nodes.title: Heat exhaustion - rest and cool
steps: Move them to shade or the coolest spot available. Have them lie down with legs slightly raised if they feel faint.
Loosen or remove extra clothing and gear.
Wet their skin and fan them.
Give cool water in sips. Add electrolytes or a pinch of salt and some sugar if available.
Rest for at least 30 minutes.
doNot: Do not let them go back to work or keep hiking until fully recovered.

options.label: Not improving, vomiting, or getting worse

nodes.prompt: Are they confused or acting strangely now?

nodes.title: Heat stroke - evacuate
steps: Get them to a hospital after cooling is under way. Continue cooling during transport if you can.
Watch their breathing. Put them on their side if they vomit or are unresponsive.
Temperature can rise again. Recheck often and recool if they get confused again.
Even if they seem fine, heat stroke damages organs. They need medical evaluation.

nodes.title: Not breathing - start CPR
steps: Start CPR immediately and use an AED if available.

nodes.title: Recovering from heat exhaustion
steps: Keep them resting in the shade and drinking for the rest of the day.
Avoid hard work in the heat until tomorrow. Work in the cooler early morning or evening.
If confusion, vomiting, or fainting starts, treat as heat stroke.

nodes.title: Not improving - get help
steps: Keep cooling and resting. Keep giving sips of fluid if they can keep it down.
Get them to medical care. Vomiting stops them from rehydrating by mouth.
Check their thinking every few minutes. Confusion means heat stroke: start aggressive cooling.
